entries.title: Midnight Ambiguous Zone
entries.description:
📍 From July to September 2026, DE Cinema presented Midnight Ambiguous Zone, a screening programme dedicated to Sinophone queer cinema in the Netherlands.

Coinciding with WorldPride Amsterdam 2026, we invited audiences to explore emotions and relationships that resist fixed labels. Through cinema, we sought to reimagine ambiguity, friendship, nights, encounters and farewells, as well as fluid forms of intimacy and ever-evolving senses of belonging.

Through these moving images from the Sinophone world, we hoped to collectively explore how queer experiences are seen, felt and discussed across different cultural and urban spaces.

🎬 Screening Schedule

📍 19 July (Sunday) | 15:30
Nowhere Bookstore | The Hague

Will You Look at Me | Dir. Huang Shuli (Queer Palm Award for Best Short Film)
Heart Murmurs | Dir. Zhang Ziyin
China PK Queen | Dir. Wei Jiangang
Quietly Tell Her | Dir. Chen Pinru

📍 24 July (Friday) | The Pulse | Amsterdam

18:30 | The Last Year of Darkness
92 min | Documentary | 2023
20:10 | Live Online Q&A with director Benjamin Mullinkosson

📍 25 July (Saturday) | The Pulse | Amsterdam

18:30 | Blue Gate Crossing
83 min | Fiction | 2002

📍 4 August (Tuesday) | KINO | Rotterdam

19:15 | Blue Gate Crossing

📍 8 September (Tuesday) | KINO | Rotterdam

19:15 | The Last Year of Darkness

entries.title: After the Last Light
entries.description:
Together with @worm.rotterdam, we are pleased to present After the Last Light, the first programme in the "Nocturnal Wonderlands" Short Film Screening Series.

The programme features a selection of short films that explore passing encounters, quiet emotion traces, and subtle moments of strangeness that surface in daily personal life after every nightfall.

Across seven short films, this programme examines the shifting relationship among vision, light, and the existence of the image.

Moving between personal memory, sensory perception, and technological environments, these films examine how images emerge at the limits of visibility.

Some turn toward blindness and the ways images can be constructed through touch, sound, and imagination. Others examine landscapes transformed by artificial illumination, where light no longer reveals the world but overwhelms it.

🎬Film Line-up
In Another Night (2024) — Yunyi Zhu
Chroma (2024) — Yunyi Zhu
Everything Near Becomes Distant (2022) — Yunyi Zhu
Look on the Bright Side (2023) - Yuyan Wang
The Moon Also Rises (2024) — Yuyan Wang
Of Dreams in the Dream of Another Mirror (2023) - Yunyi Zhu
The World Remains Our First and Last Love (2025) - Yunyi Zhu

📅Time: 1 April, 20:30
📍Location: @worm.rotterdam
Boomgaardsstraat 71, 3012 BN Rotterdam

entries.title: FIRST Curated Screening · Amsterdam | Rebuilding the Nearby
entries.description:
🎞️ “The Nearby” refers not only to physical proximity — familiar places, homes, or corners that once existed — but also to a sense of emotional intimacy: our attachment to people, memories, and past versions of ourselves.

“Reappearance” suggests the recovery, reconstruction, or return of overlooked memories. It is both an acknowledgment of what has disappeared and an attempt to awaken traces that still linger beneath the surface of the present.

Under the theme “Reappearing the Nearby,” this edition of FIRST Curated Screening · Drifting Station explores through moving images how the familiar is remembered, reimagined, and perhaps even repaired.

🎬 First Half: A Theatre of Veiled Intimacy

The first half focuses on the relationship between physical space and emotional intimacy. We have selected Shards (《锔瓷》) as our feature film. Through its confined interior settings and understated character relationships, the film intertwines the narratives of the pandemic and family life.

Here, “the nearby” refers not only to physical closeness, but also to the emotional distance between people — and to the quiet, often hesitant attempts to mend the cracks between them.

The film explores fractured relationships, moments of silence and estrangement, and the profound yet fragile possibility of reconnecting. It offers a reflection on life, marriage, and the complicated emotions we carry towards those closest to us.

📽️ Second Half: Where Space and Memory Overlap

Moving beyond the intimate and personal, the second half brings together four live-action short films and two animated shorts to explore how spaces become meeting points for emotion and time.

Here, “the nearby” is no longer simply a geographical concept, but a sense of emotional familiarity. Through films that revisit places once inhabited or longed for, this programme reveals how memory reshapes space, and how landscapes from the past leave lasting imprints on our inner worlds.

⏰ Date: 10 May 2025
📍 Venue: Ventilator Cinema (OT301, 2nd floor, Overtoom 301, Amsterdam)

entries.title: Asian Records: The B-Side of Youth
entries.description:
We're thrilled to announce the October 17 Screening, curated under the theme Asian Records: The B-Side of Youth."

What is youth, after all?

It's hard to define in a single phrase. It can be sincere, impulsive, and passionate; it can also be confused, troubled, regretful, or even dull. But one thing is certain: youth is never just about its glamorous side.

• Doors open 15:00
• @ventilator_cinema -- in collaboration with us!

Programme Highlights:
15:30 - Little Blue (Feature Film) + Director Q&A
18:10 - Short Film Collection (NL Premieres) + Director Q&A:
→ No More Gravity At Night
→ HANNYA
→ Wild Bird
→ Fly Me To The Sea
→ How I Grew Up

Subtitles: Chinese & English
In this screening program, we attempt to reconstruct the 'mainstream soundtrack of youth' expected in East Asian societies, while embracing the ambiguous states between childhood and adulthood, dependence and independence, fantasy and reality.
